migration_summary: Add a NOT NULL column with no DEFAULT to a table created in the immediately-preceding Flyway migration (V1.00). Real, verbatim SQL from the repo's own migrations/ folder.
migration_sql: ALTER TABLE customers ADD COLUMN name VARCHAR(10) NOT NULL;
schema_summary: customers table with a single existing PRIMARY KEY column (id); the migration adds a second column.

risk_flags.message: ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL with no DEFAULT has no value to backfill existing rows with; PostgreSQL rejects the statement outright on any table that already has rows, rather than running slowly.

risk_narrative: This exact statement only succeeds in the demo because V1.00 creates the customers table and V1.01 runs before any row is ever inserted — on a table with even one existing row, PostgreSQL raises `column "name" of relation "customers" contains null values` and the migration fails outright rather than degrading gracefully. This is a common first mistake when hand-writing an ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL: it works in a fresh dev database (always empty) and fails the first time it's run against anything with real data.
lessons_learned: ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL needs either a DEFAULT (cheap in modern Postgres — a metadata-only change since PG 11 for a constant default) or a separate backfill step before the constraint is added, on any table that might have existing rows. Testing a migration only against an empty database will not catch this failure mode.
surprise_notes: The statement is syntactically valid and will be accepted by any SQL linter; the failure is purely data-dependent (fails only when the target table is non-empty), which is exactly the kind of failure that a fresh empty dev/CI database won't catch before it reaches a real environment.

prediction_summary.risk_explanation: Succeeds instantly on an empty table (as in this demo); fails outright rather than running slowly on any table that already has rows, which this scale-tier/confidence estimate does not capture without knowing whether the target table is populated.

dimension_details.note: Real migration file, verbatim, from arinpro/postgresql-flyway-demo's migrations/ folder — a small demo repo, included specifically because it demonstrates a common ADD COLUMN NOT NULL mistake, not because of its scale.
